intro: New Jersey runs elections county by county, through each county clerk and county board of elections, with the Division of Elections in the Department of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Most voters do not need to show ID. If your registration is marked "need ID" because you did not give a driver's license number, state ID number, or Social Security number, you vote by provisional ballot. A voter who mails a ballot does not need to send a copy of ID, except in some first-time cases, and those voters get a notice with their ballot.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Counties set their own sites. Sites are open at least 10 am to 8 pm Monday to Saturday and 10 am to 6 pm on Sunday.

dates.label: Last day to request a mail ballot by mail
dates.detail: A mailed request must be made at least 7 days before Election Day.

src.label: New Jersey Division of Elections, voting FAQ

dates.label: Last day to get a mail ballot in person
dates.detail: You can pick up and apply for a mail ballot at your county clerk's office until 3 pm.

src.label: New Jersey Division of Elections, voting FAQ

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6 am to 8 pm. A mail ballot must be postmarked by Election Day. If you use a drop box or deliver it in person, it must arrive by 8 pm.

dates.label: Mail ballots must arrive
dates.detail: A mailed ballot postmarked by Election Day must reach your county board of elections by the sixth day after the polls close.
